rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Packed {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic packed Cobalt Strike payloads - HIGH FP RISK"
        author = "SOC Team"
        confidence = "medium"
        false_positives = "Packed legitimate .NET applications, signed Microsoft updates"
        remediation = "Whitelist known-good hashes, use in conjunction with network IOCs"
    strings:
        $s1 = "CoBaltStRiKe" ascii nocase
        $s2 = { 60 00 6D 00 73 00 68 00 65 00 6C 00 6C 00 } // "msiexec" wide
        $s3 = { 4D 5A 90 00 03 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 ?? ?? 00 00 } // MZ header + PE
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and filesize < 500KB and
        (all of ($s*))
}

// Updated to exclude known Microsoft-signed binaries
import "pe"

condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and
    filesize < 500KB and
    all of ($s*) and
    not pe.imphash() == "d7a9e8e7a9e8e7a9e8e7a9e8e7a9e8e7" and
    not pe.cert_valid() and
    not pe.company_name == "Microsoft Corporation"

This incident highlights detection blind spots, response misalignment, and the need for improved IOA-based alerting.
